summary: This joint resolution nullifies the IRS rule on gross proceeds reporting by brokers for digital asset sales by invoking the Congressional Review Act to disapprove the December 2024 regulation.

scores.thoughts: The bill disapproves an IRS reporting rule on digital asset transactions. It has no provisions related to government expenditures, appropriations, or budget outlays.

The legislation uses the Congressional Review Act to nullify an IRS rule requiring brokers to report gross proceeds from digital asset sales. This directly blocks expanded tax-reporting and compliance requirements for cryptocurrency transactions, reducing the administrative burden and enforcement mechanisms associated with taxation of digital assets.
No provisions in the bill address healthcare policy, insurance, public health programs, or medical regulation.
The bill contains no language concerning firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No references to immigration policy, border security, visas, or related enforcement.
The resolution does not address reproductive rights, abortion access, or related regulations.
No content related to military funding, defense programs, or national security appropriations.
The bill has no bearing on environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy standards.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other social safety-net entitlements.
The legislation does not engage with education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
No references to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance regulations.
The bill does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions relate to tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
While the blocked rule could indirectly affect tax revenue collection, the bill itself makes no explicit statement on deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal targets.
No content concerning LGBTQ protections or related civil rights measures.
The resolution contains no provisions on foreign assistance or international aid.
No engagement with voting rights, election administration, or electoral integrity measures.
Although the underlying IRS rule concerns digital assets, the bill addresses only tax-reporting obligations and does not regulate technology platforms, data privacy standards, or surveillance.
No provisions address labor rights, union organizing, or workplace regulations.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions, anti-discrimination law, or civil-rights balancing.
